## Context / Problem
`tests/unit/test_mcp_entrypoint_provisioning.py::test_a_peer_finishing_the_clone_while_we_wait_skips_the_redundant_reclone` failed in `make verify` on 2026-11-04 PST (worktree fix-caudata, commit `ff107f59ce2`, change for `asthmatic-grave-caudata`, which touches only `src/rebar/_store/{paths,compat}.py`, a new test, and docs). This is an assertion failure, not a worker crash:

`AssertionError: lock holder must re-probe HEAD before re-cloning`. The script stderr held only `mcp: tickets store provisioning finished`, with returncode 0 and no `was re-cloned by another container` line.

Observations:
- The full run took 2 h 11 min at host load average about 29 to 31.
- Run alone 10 times afterwards at load average 31: 10 passed, 0 failed.
- `stellar-sane-hawk` (closed) recorded the same test failing once under `make verify` and passing alone. Its closing root cause was a 3 s pytest-timeout in a different test (`test_review_bot.py`) crashing the worker. That cause does not produce this assertion message, so it does not cover this failure.

Hypotheses (unproven): the peer callback releases the lock after the script has already stopped waiting or taken a different branch under scheduler load; the second HEAD probe runs before `head-resolves` is visible; something else.

## Approach
Reproduce under xdist with the neighbouring module order, adding a log of the fake-git call sequence and the lock-wait timing to the failure message. Confirm which branch the script took before changing the test or the script.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The failing branch is identified with recorded evidence (git call sequence and timing) in a comment on this ticket.
- [ ] The test is deterministic under `make test` without weakening the re-probe assertion, shown by 1 full `make test` run that passes this test on a loaded host.
compiled_state.title: MCP entrypoint peer-finished-clone test misses the re-probe message under a loaded make verify
